title: A Cross-Analyzing Approach to Sentiment and Bias Detection in Social Media: Insights from Geopolitical Conflicts
problem: During geopolitical conflicts, social-media discourse is contaminated by sentiment polarisation and systemic bias, making impartial situational awareness extremely difficult.
methodology: Compared BERT and BiLSTM approaches for sentiment and bias detection in social-media discourse about geopolitical conflicts, using WordPiece and GloVe representations.
impact: The paper reports comparative results for sentiment classification and bias detection, highlighting the different strengths of the two approaches.
description: Cross-analysing pipeline for sentiment and bias in geopolitical social-media discourse — surfacing measurable bias signals during conflict events.

title: Improving Monkeypox Outbreak Prediction Through Time-Series Forecasting with Machine Learning Models
problem: Public-health agencies needed earlier, more reliable forecasts of Monkeypox outbreak trajectories to plan response and allocation.
methodology: Compared XGBoost, LSTM and Prophet on monkeypox death time-series data from 2019–2023, with lag and rolling-window features.
impact: The study reports the lowest mean squared error among the compared models for Prophet (0.4175), within its experimental setup.
description: Comparative time-series forecasting of monkeypox deaths using XGBoost, LSTM and Prophet.
